primary_claim: Across most broad OLMo SFT behaviors (bold formatting, both-sides framing, liberal-lean, validating feelings, etc.), targeted data filtering using training-data-attribution methods (LLM autoraters, probes, activation-based methods, EKFAC) removes documents identified as most responsible for a behavior but does not reduce that behavior any more than removing random documents; refusal is the only behavior found to be reliably filterable.

effect.metric: behavior-eval score reduction from top-10%/25% document removal vs random-removal baseline
effect.value: TDA-based filtering does not significantly outperform random removal for most behaviors (e.g. 'Your feelings are valid' rate unchanged despite removing top 10% of attributed documents); refusal is reduced significantly by probes/LLM judges

depends_on: arXiv:2506.11613 (Turner et al. 2025, risky-finance emergent-misalignment dataset)
contradicts_or_qualifies: Contradicts the natural prior assumption that undesired SFT behaviors can be controlled by identifying and filtering the responsible training documents
limitations_stated: Due to compute constraints, work uses a lower-cost 'speed-run' version of OLMo SFT (rank-64 LoRA on a 1% stratified sample of the SFT dataset) rather than the full training pipeline
EKFAC costs are dominated by an initial fit-factors step that is behavior agnostic
Judgements of insane/garbled responses have not been validated by a human judge
quote: To our surprise, across most of our broad OLMo SFT behaviors, data filtering often has very little effect.
